claims.title: Duplicate detection can suppress a legitimate review with different inline comments
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**Duplicate detection can suppress a legitimate review with different inline comments**

Confidence: 90

`findMatchingReview()` treats any existing review with the same `commit_id` and top-level `body` as proof that the failed POST already landed. That is not strong enough to establish byte-for-byte identity of the review being retried: two reviews on the same commit can legitimately share the same summary body while carrying different `comments`. In that case this retry path would incorrectly return the older review ID and skip posting the new findings.

This is a correctness regression in the new idempotency check. To make the retry safe, the match needs to include the review's inline comments as well, or the request needs its own idempotency token that can be searched for unambiguously.

claims.title: Matching only on commit_id + body is not sufficient to prove the failed POST landed
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**Matching only on commit_id + body is not sufficient to prove the failed POST landed**

This lookup can return a false positive when the PR already has another review on the same commit with the same summary body but different inline comments. In that case the retry loop will conclude the POST succeeded, return `match.id`, and never create the current review's comments. Users will be confused because the run reports success while findings are silently missing.

Given the repository's no-silent-failure standard, this needs a stronger identity check than `commit_id + body` alone, or the code should treat such matches as ambiguous and fall back instead of claiming success.

claims.title: Matching on body alone can misidentify a different review as the retried POST
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**Matching on body alone can misidentify a different review as the retried POST**

This lookup only compares `commit_id` and `body`, but review creation also includes `comments`. On the same PR head commit, two different reviews can legitimately share the same summary body while having different inline comments. In that case a failed POST would be treated as already-landed and the new review would never be posted, dropping findings. The match criteria here need to include the inline comments payload (or another exact idempotency marker), not just the top-level body.

claims.title: Duplicate detection can suppress a distinct review with the same summary body
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**Duplicate detection can suppress a distinct review with the same summary body**

This lookup treats any existing review on the same commit with the same top-level `body` as proof that the failed POST already landed. That is safe only if `body` uniquely identifies the full review payload, but review submissions also include `event` and inline `comments`. If two different reviews on the same commit share the same body text but differ in their inline comments, this code will return the old review ID and skip posting the new findings entirely. The bug this PR fixes is about retries within one submission, but the matching key here is broad enough to create false positives across earlier reviews on the same commit.

claims.title: Stale doc comment describes the old return contract
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**Stale doc comment describes the old return contract**

The block comment immediately above `ReviewLookupResult` still says `findMatchingReview()` "Returns null on any lookup failure", but the implementation now distinguishes `checked: false` from `checked: true, reviewId: null`. That mismatch is likely to mislead a future maintainer into treating lookup failures as confirmed absence, which is the exact correctness distinction this patch is trying to preserve.

replies.author: joeblackwaslike
replies.body: Fixed in 2bfac5b — replaced commit_id+body equality with a per-attempt marker (invisible HTML comment, same technique as quotaCommentMarker/rateLimitCommentMarker in notify.ts), fully paginated. This closes both the whitespace-drift false-negative risk and the coincidental-match-against-an-unrelated-review risk in one change — see the commit message for the full rationale.
